speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned gait and limb ataxia; to better understand your condition, have you experienced any weakness, numbness, or changes in your vision recently? Also, what was the most significant medical event in your history leading up to these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that description; the "drunk" appearance often suggests cerebellar involvement. Given your significant medical history, have you ever been diagnosed with multiple sclerosis, syphilis, or had a stroke? Also, do you notice any double vision or difficulty speaking?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) secondary to natalizumab therapy in a patient with Crohn's disease.

I recommend immediately holding the natalizumab and requesting an MRI of the brain with and without contrast to confirm the presence of non-enhancing white matter lesions, along with a JC Virus antibody test.
